draft.title: Strong and weak acids
card: An acid that ionises fully in water. Almost every molecule donates its proton, so the solution holds mostly ions. Hydrochloric acid, HCl, is an example.
An acid that ionises only partly in water. Most molecules stay unchanged, and an equilibrium forms. Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is an example.
Strength is about how far an acid ionises. Concentration is about how much acid is dissolved in a given volume of solution. They are separate ideas.
A concentrated solution has a lot of acid in it. A dilute solution has little. Either kind of solution can be made from a strong acid or from a weak acid.
draft.remember: Strength is how much of the acid ionises. Concentration is how much acid is dissolved.

a.q: What makes hydrochloric acid a strong acid?
opts: It ionises almost fully when dissolved in water
It is dissolved at a high concentration in water
It contains more hydrogen atoms than a weak acid
It forms an equilibrium with most molecules unchanged
a.why: A strong acid is defined by how far it ionises, and HCl ionises almost fully. Concentration is a different idea, because a strong acid can be dilute and a weak acid can be concentrated.
a.clue: Strength describes what happens to each molecule in water.

b.q: Sam has 0.1 mol L⁻¹ ethanoic acid and 0.001 mol L⁻¹ hydrochloric acid. Which statement about them is correct?
opts: Ethanoic acid is weak and more concentrated
Ethanoic acid is strong and more concentrated
Hydrochloric acid is weak and more dilute
Hydrochloric acid is strong and more concentrated
b.why: Ethanoic acid ionises only partly, so it is weak, and 0.1 mol L⁻¹ is a greater concentration than 0.001 mol L⁻¹. Concentration does not decide strength, so the more concentrated acid is not the stronger one.
b.clue: Judge strength and concentration separately, one at a time.

a.best: It ionises almost fully when dissolved in water

b.best: Ethanoic acid is weak and more concentrated
